title: Disconnect Path in a Binary Matrix by at Most One Flip
summary: Given a 0-indexed m x n binary matrix grid, determine if it is possible to make the matrix disconnected from the cell (0, 0) to the cell (m - 1, n - 1) by flipping the value of at most one cell (excluding the start and end cells).
statement: Given a 0-indexed m x n binary matrix grid, determine if it is possible to make the matrix disconnected from the cell (0, 0) to the cell (m - 1, n - 1) by flipping the value of at most one cell (excluding the start and end cells). Flipping a cell changes its value from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0. Return true if the path can be disconnected, otherwise return false.
constraints: Movement from the top-left to bottom-right is only down or right through cells containing one.
You may flip at most one cell other than the endpoints.
Return whether all such paths can be destroyed.
hints: First find one down-right path and erase its internal cells during DFS.
Restore the protected endpoints, then search again.
If a second path exists after removing the first, no single internal cell intersects every path.
Conversely, if no second path exists, one cell on the erased route is a separator, so the two DFS passes characterize one-flip disconnectability.
editorial: Conversely, if no second path exists, one cell on the erased route is a separator, so the two DFS passes characterize one-flip disconnectability.

tests.explanation: Every path uses a removable bottleneck, so one flip disconnects the endpoints.
Two internally disjoint routes remain, so one flip cannot disconnect them.
